items.note: Based on YourMechanic (about $118 parts and $95 labor on average; per-year estimates about $332–$352). Owners say the parts are easy to reach.

items.note: YourMechanic lists about $1,040 to $1,050 for fuel pump work on the turbo Solstice. One TrueDelta owner paid a dealer $860 for a new high-pressure pump.
items.t: Reduced power from a failing high-pressure fuel pump

items.job: Replace camshaft position actuator or solenoid
items.note: TrueDelta owners report about $80 for a pair of cam actuators and $600 for a timing chain, tensioner and guides. A dealer will usually charge more.
items.t: Camshaft timing codes from actuators or a stretched chain

items.note: YourMechanic lists about $400 to $515 for a thermostat on these cars. A new cooling fan adds parts cost.
items.t: Overheating from a failed cooling fan or thermostat

items.job: Adjust or replace parking brake cable
items.note: One TrueDelta owner paid $156 for a rear caliper parking brake teardown done along with recall work. Rear caliper replacement costs more.
YourMechanic lists about $2,150 to $2,270 for a compressor. A hose or condenser repair is cheaper.

items.t: Check engine light from the gas cap

items.note: Based on YourMechanic (about $312 parts and $224 labor on average). Its per-year estimates run about $857–$1,344 per pair. The right part depends on the suspension package code on the glove box sticker.
